pull_request.title: chore: move cargo-cost-lint to edition 2024 and collapse nested if-let chain
pull_request.body:
## Summary

This PR moves `cargo-cost-lint` to Rust edition 2024, aligning it with `soroban_cost_lints` and the rest of the workspace. It also collapses the three-deep nested `if let` chain in the config parsing block into edition-2024 let-chains, matching the convention described in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the style already used in `soroban_cost_lints/src/lib.rs`.

## Changes

### 1. `cargo-cost-lint/Cargo.toml`
- Changed `edition` from `2021` to `2024`

### 2. `cargo-cost-lint/src/main.rs`
- Replaced the three-deep nested `if let` block with an edition-2024 let-chain using `if let ... && let ... && let ...`
- Extracted `config_path` binding to avoid calling `resolve_config` twice
- Matches the convention described in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the style already used in `soroban_cost_lints/src/lib.rs`

### Behavior Note

There is one minor behavioral difference: in the original code, a `fs::read_to_string` failure was silently swallowed (only TOML parse errors triggered the warning). In the let-chain version, both read errors and parse errors hit the `else if` branch and produce a warning. This is an improvement — a config file that exists but can't be read should produce feedback — and the overall behavior (falling back to default lint levels) is identical.

## Verification

- [x] `cargo-cost-lint/Cargo.toml` edition is now `2024`
- [x] Nested if-let chain collapsed into let-chains
- [x] Matches the style used in `soroban_cost_lints/src/lib.rs`
- [ ] CI: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [ ] CI: `cargo test --workspace`
- [ ] CI: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

Closes #83
